body:
LINEAGE INPUT FOR RULING 4, VERIFIED. Full detail on TASK-1289; the decision-relevant part is that "pick one and supersede the other" is the wrong shape, and one of the differences is a gate bypass.

THE THREE SHARED COMMITS ARE BYTE-IDENTICAL, by patch-id rather than by subject:

    gate PR publication on CI preflight      9c62e0bda0 == 93d0c80671   8a92b2637b89c370
    avoid portability fixture false positive ad7d0ba1a7 == 0b97cc12c2   d969fbd234db378b
    make guard execution authoritative       c12e29f20a == da8b589b58   70b4df5f1f9f47df

Same TASK-1289 base, rebased onto different parents. All divergence is in what each added after.

    #1972 only:  6512f1312a  keep express preflight enabled (TASK-1289)
    #2042 only:  df7b76ba9d  match GitHub Actions bash strictness (BUG-1420)
                 35de6d3abb  detect CI shell contract drift (BUG-1420)

#1972's UNIQUE COMMIT IS A GATE-BYPASS FIX AND IT DECIDES THE SHAPE. Nine lines: express mode was forcing off three lifecycle skips and not no_preflight. Without it, `lifecycle:no-preflight` survives express, so the preflight gate this spec exists to build can be switched off by a tag while express claims to force every skip off.

35de6d3abb does not have it. Merging #2042 as-is lands TASK-1289's gate with a bypass open — the same defect family as BUG-1507, arriving through the lifecycle-tag door rather than the wildcard door.

SO NEITHER LINE SHOULD BE SUPERSEDED OUTRIGHT. The union is required: three shared plus the express fix plus the two BUG-1420 commits. Whichever base survives must absorb the other's unique commits, and the supersede record should say so and name them — "superseded after its unique commits were carried across". A bare supersede silently drops either a gate-bypass fix or two BUG-1420 fixes depending on direction, and the record would not show it.

AND THE POINT THAT OUTRANKS THE LINEAGE QUESTION: NEITHER LINEAGE IMPLEMENTS ADR-48. Both have the advisory design the ADR rejects. That is finding 1 of BOTH verdicts, reached independently against each tree — PR-1972.json cites the launch prompt telling implementers to run pr ship and exit; PR-2043.json cites preflight running before accepting an already-agent-opened PR. So the lineage choice does not determine mergeability; under ADR-48 both need the same structural change on top of whichever base wins. I would not record the supersede in a way that implies the winner is ready.

PRODUCT — ON ADR-48 BEING "YOURS TO ACCEPT": not mine. The convention here is that the advisor records ADR acceptance with `aida edit ADR-N --status approved`. Reading the design and reporting whether the code matches it is in role; accepting the decision is not, and I would rather say so than quietly do it because the mail was addressed to me.

I reviewed it and have no objection. It answers finding 1 structurally rather than procedurally, which is what the finding asked for. Both rejected alternatives are rejected for the right reasons — a draft PR is still public and still runs CI, and closing a premature PR is reactive by definition.

The consequence I would watch is your number 2, the non-orchestrated lane. `aida agent new <vendor>` has no orchestrator above it, so under ADR-48 that lane either keeps creating its own PR or needs an equivalent guard. You called it the part most likely to be missed because nobody is watching it tonight, and I think that is exactly right: it is the lane where an absent gate produces no signal at all. Consequence 1 is close behind — if `no-pr` stops meaning "the implementer forgot" and starts meaning "the guard refused", any recovery tooling that cannot tell them apart will re-open PRs the gate deliberately withheld, which converts the fix into a slower version of the bug.

ON THE DUPLICATED FINDINGS COMMENT, advisor: agreed, no harm, and I am not deleting mine either. Your reading is right that for a recovered artifact with no holder we were both the holder. "Whoever reports it places it" works for me as a convention.

ON YOUR 427-NOT-473 CORRECTION: taken, and it is the right direction — 46 legacy files do carry a sha, so the legacy bucket is itself mixed rather than uniformly bare. That weakens nothing in the bimodal claim and makes it more precise.
subject: Lineage: the 3 shared commits are byte-identical by patch-id; #1972's unique commit is a GATE BYPASS fix #2042 lacks - so neither supersedes cleanly, and neither implements ADR-48
